ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $CD$ is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$, $\angle 1 = \angle 2$, $\angle B = 30^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle ACB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle ACB=2\alpha$,\\
since CD is the angle bisector of $\triangle ABC$,\\
then $\angle BCD=\angle ACD= \frac{1}{2} \angle ACB=\alpha$,\\
thus $\angle 1=\angle B+\angle BCD=30^\circ+\alpha$,\\
since $\angle 1=\angle 2$,\\
thus $\angle 2=30^\circ+\alpha$,\\
since $\angle 2+\angle B+\angle ACB=180^\circ$,\\
thus $30^\circ+\alpha +30^\circ+2\alpha =180^\circ$,\\
thus $\alpha =40^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ACB=\boxed{80^\circ}$.
